These charts show the groups that political parties target with their advertisements leading up to the elections, according to the latest data. The focus is on Meta's platforms (Facebook and Instagram) because they offer the most detailed targeting options for political advertisements.

How much did the campaigns of political parties spend on different audiences? The charts below show both the total and the expenditures per party.

> Note: Different targeting criteria may overlap, so the outcome may not necessarily add up to 100%.



::: {.panel-tabset}

::: {.panel-tabset}



#### Total


```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, dpi=300}


library(tidytable)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(highcharter)
library(tidyr) # For complete()
library(forcats) # For fct_reorder()

# Assuming election_dat30, calc_targeting, and currency_symbol are available

# This is your original data preparation for party-level analysis
# It remains unchanged.
election_dat30 <- election_dat30 %>% 
    mutate(total_spend = total_spend_formatted) 

col_each30 <- election_dat30 %>%
    mutate(cntry_party = paste0(cntry, "XXXXXXX", party)) %>% 
    pull(cntry_party) %>% 
    unique() %>% 
    map_dfr(~{
      important <- str_split(.x, "XXXXXXX") %>% unlist()
      the_dat <- election_dat30 %>% filter(cntry == important[1]) %>% filter(party == important[2])  
      
      calc_targeting(the_dat) %>%
        mutate(
          party = the_dat$party[1],
          internal_id = the_dat$internal_id[1],
          cntry = the_dat$cntry[1])
    }, .progress = T) %>% 
    filter(target != "Gender: All") %>% 
    filter(target != "Unknown")

# --- START: New Block to get Page-Level Spend by Target Method ---

# As per your suggestion, we run `calc_targeting` on each page to get the needed detail.
page_spend_by_target <- election_dat30 %>%
  # Create a unique identifier for each page to iterate over
  mutate(cntry_page = paste0(cntry, "XXXXXXX", page_name)) %>%
  pull(cntry_page) %>%
  unique() %>%
  map_dfr(~{
    # Deconstruct the identifier safely
    important <- str_split(.x, "XXXXXXX", n = 2) %>% unlist()
    page_country <- important[1]
    page_name_filter <- important[2]
    
    # Filter the main dataset for this specific page
    the_page_dat <- election_dat30 %>% 
      filter(cntry == page_country, page_name == page_name_filter)
      
    # If the page has data, run calc_targeting and add back identifiers
    if(nrow(the_page_dat) > 0) {
      calc_targeting(the_page_dat) %>%
        mutate(
          page_name = page_name_filter,
          party = the_page_dat$party[1] 
        )
    }
  }, .progress = TRUE)

# --- END: Page-Level Spend Block ---

# This is your original data preparation for the plot
all_spend <- col_each30  %>% 
    distinct(internal_id, .keep_all = T) %>% 
    summarise(total = sum(total),
              total_ads = sum(total_ads))

# --- THIS BLOCK IS NOW FIXED ---
gg <- col_each30  %>%
    filter(target != "countries") %>% 
    add_count(target) %>%
    mutate(target_clean = case_when(
        target == "custom_audience" ~ "Custom Audiences (Internal Data)",
        target == "custom_audience_thirdparty" ~ "Custom Audiences (Uploaded Data)",
        target == "countries" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Entire Country",
        target == "regions" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Regions",
        target == "lookalike_audience" ~ "Lookalike Audiences",
        target == "interest" ~ "Detailed",
        target == "age" ~ "Age",
        target == "zips" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Postal Code",
        target == "CITY" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: City",
        target == "language" ~ "Language",
        target == "gender" ~ "Gender",
        target == "COMUNE" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Municipality",
        target == "electoral_districts" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Electoral Districts",
        target == "COUNTY" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Counties",
        str_detect(target, "NEIGHBOR") ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Neighborhood",
        T ~ target
    )) %>%
    filter(target_clean != "Unknown") %>%
    group_by(target_clean) %>% # FIX: Group by the new, clean column name
    summarize(spend_per = sum(spend_per)) %>% 
    rename(target = target_clean) %>% # FIX: Rename the column *after* the summary
    mutate(perc = spend_per/all_spend$total*100) %>% 
    arrange(desc(perc)) %>% 
    filter(perc >= 0.01)

# --- START: New Block for Tooltip Generation ---

# 1. In our new detailed data, clean the target names to match the plot data `gg`.
page_spend_by_target_renamed <- page_spend_by_target %>%
  mutate(target = case_when(
    target == "custom_audience" ~ "Custom Audiences (Internal Data)",
    target == "custom_audience_thirdparty" ~ "Custom Audiences (Uploaded Data)",
    target == "countries" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Entire Country",
    target == "regions" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Regions",
    target == "lookalike_audience" ~ "Lookalike Audiences",
    target == "interest" ~ "Detailed",
    target == "age" ~ "Age",
    target == "zips" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Postal Code",
    target == "CITY" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: City",
    target == "language" ~ "Language",
    target == "gender" ~ "Gender",
    target == "COMUNE" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Municipality",
    target == "electoral_districts" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Electoral Districts",
    target == "COUNTY" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Counties",
    str_detect(target, "NEIGHBOR") ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Neighborhood",
    T ~ target
  ))

# 2. Use a FOR loop to generate the tooltip HTML for each target method in `gg`.
tooltip_list <- vector("character", nrow(gg))

for (i in 1:nrow(gg)) {
  current_target <- gg$target[i]
  total_spend_for_method <- gg$spend_per[i]

  # Find top spending pages for the current target method.
  top_pages <- page_spend_by_target_renamed %>%
    filter(target == current_target, spend_per > 0) %>%
    arrange(-spend_per) %>%
    slice_head(n = 5) %>% # Show up to top 5 pages
    mutate(perc_of_method_spend = (spend_per / total_spend_for_method) * 100) %>%
    filter(!is.na(page_name))

  if (nrow(top_pages) > 0) {
    page_strings <- apply(top_pages, 1, function(row) {
      sprintf("&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;• %s: %s (%.1f%%)",
              row["page_name"],
              scales::comma(round(as.numeric(row["spend_per"])), prefix = currency_symbol),
              as.numeric(row["perc_of_method_spend"]))
    })
    
    num_pages <- nrow(top_pages)
    header_text <- paste0("Top ", num_pages, " page", if(num_pages > 1) "s", " using this method:")
    
    tooltip_list[i] <- paste0("<br><br><b>", header_text, "</b><br>", paste(page_strings, collapse = "<br>"))
  } else {
    tooltip_list[i] <- ""
  }
}

# 3. Add the generated tooltip strings as a column to the plot data `gg`.
gg_with_tooltip <- gg %>%
  mutate(tooltip_pages_html = tooltip_list)

# --- END: Tooltip Generation Block ---

# Your original plotting code, now using the enhanced data
the_order <- gg_with_tooltip %>%
  tidyr::complete(target, fill = list(perc = 0)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(target = forcats::fct_reorder(target, perc, .desc = FALSE)) %>%
  dplyr::pull(target) %>%
  levels()

gg_with_tooltip %>%
  mutate(spend_perlab = scales::comma(round(spend_per))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(target = forcats::fct_relevel(target, the_order)) %>%
  highcharter::hchart(type = "bar", hcaes(x = target, y = perc)) %>%
  highcharter::hc_plotOptions(bar = list(color = "darkgrey")) %>%
  highcharter::hc_xAxis(labels = list(style = list(fontSize = "10px"))) %>%
  highcharter::hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Budget spent on targeting method (% of total spend)")) %>%
  highcharter::hc_add_theme(hc_theme_google()) %>%
  highcharter::hc_tooltip(
    pointFormat = paste0(
        "<b>{point.target}</b>",
        "<br>% of total budget spent: {point.y:.1f}%",
        "<br>A total of ", currency_symbol, "{point.spend_perlab} on this method.",
        "{point.tooltip_pages_html}" # <-- This adds the new info
    ),
    headerFormat = "",
    useHTML = TRUE
  ) %>%
  highcharter::hc_credits(
    enabled = TRUE,
    text = "Source: Meta Ad Library. Data Viz: Fabio Votta (@favstats)."
  ) %>%
  hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE) %>% 
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = ""))






```


#### By Party

```{r}
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)

# Assuming color_dat and currency_symbol are available in your environment
# And `page_spend_by_target_renamed` exists and has columns:
# party, page_name, target (cleaned names), spend_per

plot_geography <- function(x, page_spend_detail) {
  # x <- col_each30
  # page_spend_detail is your pre-existing page_spend_by_target_renamed
  
  # Your original logic to create the main plot data. This is unchanged.
  gg <- x %>%
    filter(target != "countries") %>% 
    group_by(target, party) %>% 
    summarize(spend_per = sum(spend_per),
              total = sum(total))  %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    mutate(perc = spend_per/total*100) %>%
    filter(perc >= 0.5) %>%
    mutate(target = case_when(
      target == "custom_audience" ~ "Custom Audiences (Internal Data)",
      target == "custom_audience_thirdparty" ~ "Custom Audiences (Uploaded Data)",
      target == "countries" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Entire Country",
      target == "regions" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Regions",
      target == "lookalike_audience" ~ "Lookalike Audiences",
      target == "interest" ~ "Detailed",
      target == "age" ~ "Age",
      target == "zips" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Postal Code",
      target == "CITY" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: City",
      target == "language" ~ "Language",
      target == "gender" ~ "Gender",
      target == "COMUNE" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Municipality",
      target == "electoral_districts" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Electoral Districts",
      target == "COUNTY" ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Counties",
      str_detect(target, "NEIGHBOR") ~ "GEOGRAPHY: Neighborhood",
      TRUE ~ target
    )) %>%
    filter(target != "Unknown") %>%
    add_count(party, target) %>% 
    arrange(desc(n))

  charts <- gg %>%
    mutate(spend_perlab = scales::comma(round(spend_per))) %>%
    split(.$party) %>%
    map(~ {
      .x_party_data <- .x
      the_color <- color_dat$colors[color_dat$party == .x_party_data$party[1]]
      
      # --- START: Corrected Tooltip generation for this specific party ---
      tooltip_list <- vector("character", nrow(.x_party_data))
      
      for (i in 1:nrow(.x_party_data)) {
        current_row <- .x_party_data[i, ]
        current_party_name <- current_row$party
        current_target_name <- current_row$target
        # The total spend for the party on this specific method (the value of the bar)
        total_spend_for_criterion <- current_row$spend_per

        # Filter the detailed page data using the clean target name
        top_pages <- page_spend_detail %>%
          filter(party == current_party_name, target == current_target_name) %>%
          arrange(desc(spend_per)) %>%
          slice_head(n = 3)
          
        if (nrow(top_pages) > 0) {
          
          # Add the percentage calculation
          top_pages_with_perc <- top_pages %>%
            mutate(
              perc_of_criterion = (spend_per / total_spend_for_criterion) * 100
            )
            
          page_strings <- apply(top_pages_with_perc, 1, function(row) {
            # Update the sprintf string to include the new percentage
            sprintf("&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;• %s: %s (%.1f%%)",
                    row["page_name"],
                    scales::comma(round(as.numeric(row["spend_per"])), prefix = currency_symbol),
                    as.numeric(row["perc_of_criterion"]))
          })

          header_text <- paste0("Top ", nrow(top_pages), " Page", if(nrow(top_pages) > 1) "s", " using this method:")
          tooltip_list[i] <- paste0("<br><br><b>", header_text, "</b><br>", paste(page_strings, collapse = "<br>"))
        } else {
          tooltip_list[i] <- ""
        }
      }
      
      data_with_tooltips <- .x_party_data %>%
        mutate(tooltip_pages_html = tooltip_list)
      # --- END: Tooltip generation ---
      
      # Original logic for ordering the bars
      the_order <- data_with_tooltips %>%
        filter(party == data_with_tooltips$party[1]) %>% 
        arrange(desc(perc)) %>% 
        mutate(target = fct_reorder(target, perc, .desc = T)) %>%
        pull(target) %>%
        levels()
      
      daaat <- data_with_tooltips %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(target = as.factor(target)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(target = factor(target, levels =  the_order)) %>% 
        arrange(target)
      
      # Final plot call using the data that now includes the tooltip HTML
      hchart(daaat, type = "bar", hcaes(x = target, y = perc), color = the_color) %>%
        hc_plotOptions(bar = list(horizontal = TRUE, stacking = "normal")) %>%
        hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "% party budget spent on targeting method"), max = 100, min = 0) %>%
        hc_xAxis(title = "", labels = list(style = list(fontSize = "10px"))) %>%
        hc_add_theme(hc_theme_google()) %>%
        highcharter::hc_tooltip(
          pointFormat = paste0(
            "<b>{point.target}</b>",
            "<br>% of total budget spent: {point.y:.1f}%",
            "<br>A total of ", currency_symbol, "{point.spend_perlab} on this method.",
            "{point.tooltip_pages_html}" # <-- This adds the new info
          ),
          headerFormat = "",
          useHTML = TRUE
        ) %>%
        hc_title(text = unique(daaat$party), align = "left", style = list(fontWeight = "bold")) %>%
        hc_size(height = 300) %>%
        hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE)
    })
  
  charts
}

```


```{r echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
library(htmltools)
library(purrr)

# Generate plots
plots <- plot_geography(col_each30, page_spend_by_target_renamed)

# Map each plot to a column
columns <- map(plots, ~ div(style = "width: 50%; float: left;", .x))

# If there's an odd number of plots, add an empty div to the end to balance the columns
if (length(columns) %% 2 == 1) {
  columns <- c(columns, list(div(style = "width: 50%; float: left;")))
}

# Pair up the columns and wrap them in rows
rows <- map(seq(from = 1, to = length(columns), by = 2), ~ {
  div(class = "row",
    list(
      columns[[.x]],
      columns[[.x + 1]]
    )
  )
})

# Print the rows
tags$div(class = "container", do.call(tags$div, rows))


```

columns <- map(plots, ~ div(style = "width: 50%; float: left;", .x))

      columns[[.x + 1]]
    )
  )
})

# Print the rows
tags$div(class = "container", do.call(tags$div, rows))

overall_spend <- col_each30 %>% 
  filter(target != "countries") %>% 
  group_by(internal_id) %>% 
  arrange(desc(perc)) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  summarize(spend_per = sum(spend_per),
            total = sum(total))  %>% 
  mutate(perc = spend_per/total*100) %>% 
  filter(max(perc) == perc) %>% 
  mutate(max_calc = case_when(
    # max(perc_ads)==perc_ads ~  "Percentage of ads with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion",
    max(perc)==perc ~  "Percentage"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(val = case_when(
    # max_calc == "Percentage of ads with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion" ~ perc_ads,
    max_calc == "Percentage" ~ perc
  )) %>% 
  mutate(
    labb = case_when(
      # max_calc == "Percentage of ads with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion" ~ glue::glue("{round(perc_ads,2)}%\n({ads_per} out of {total_ads} total ads)"),
      max_calc == "Percentage" ~ glue::glue("{round(perc,2)}%\n(€{scales::number_format()(round(spend_per))} out of €{scales::number_format()(total)})"))) 


hchart(overall_spend, type = "bar", hcaes(x = max_calc, y = perc), color = "grey") %>%
            hc_plotOptions(bar = list(horizontal = TRUE, stacking = "normal")) %>%
            hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "% party budget spent on targeting method"), max = 100, min = 0) %>%
            hc_xAxis(title = "", labels = list(style = list(fontSize = "10px"))) %>%
            hc_add_theme(hc_theme_google()) %>%
           highcharter::hc_tooltip(
              pointFormat = paste0("<b>At Least One Targeting/Exclusion Criterion</b><br>% of total budget spent: {point.y:.1f}%<br>a total of ", currency_symbol,           "{point.spend_perlab} on ad with at least one targeting or exclusion criterion."),
              headerFormat = ""
            ) %>%
            hc_title(text = "Percentage of ad budget spent with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion", align = "left", style = list(fontWeight = "bold")) %>%
        hc_size(height = 300) %>%
    hc_exporting(
      enabled = TRUE
    )

  ungroup() %>% 
  # arrange(desc(perc_ads)) %>% 
  mutate(perc = spend_per/total*100) %>% 
  group_by(party) %>% 
      filter(max(perc)==perc) %>% 
  mutate(max_calc = case_when(
    # max(perc_ads)==perc_ads ~  "Percentage of ads with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion",
    max(perc)==perc ~  "Percentage of ad budget spent with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(val = case_when(
    # max_calc == "Percentage of ads with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion" ~ perc_ads,
    max_calc == "Percentage of ad budget spent with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion" ~ perc
  )) %>% 
  mutate(
    labb = case_when(
      # max_calc == "Percentage of ads with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion" ~ glue::glue("{round(perc_ads,2)}% ({ads_per} out of {total_ads})"),
      max_calc == "Percentage of ad budget spent with at least\none targeting/exclusion criterion" ~ glue::glue("{round(perc,2)}% (€{scales::number_format()(round(spend_per))})"))) %>% 
  distinct(party, .keep_all = T) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(party = fct_reorder(party, val)) %>%
